# Animate's measured rows are uniform, its items are not

## Context

`list.plugin.Animate`'s measured mode (`#18604`: owner `itemHeight: null` + `measureItemHeight: true`) takes the tallest rendered item as the list's one row height. Tried on its first real consumer today — the Institution's fleet roster (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#128) — it splits in two:

- **Homogeneous items** (the calm roster, every card the same anatomy): 126 px fixed rows become 104 px, no dead reserve. The intended win.
- **Mixed items** (one card shows a control-status row, another a two-line lane): the pitch follows the tallest card *in the whole list* while every other card stays as tall as its own content. Short cards float in tall slots — the gaps read as cards again, the defect the consumer ticket set out to remove.

Operator design ruling on the captures (2026-09-18): **cards in a grid have the same height.**

## The Problem

The mode measures items, so it cannot size them: `createItem` writes no inline height in measured mode on purpose (`Animate.mjs`, "no inline height: the item is as tall as its content, which is what gets measured"). A written height would be what the next measurement reads — in both directions: an element with an inline `height` answers a rect read with that height whatever its content does, so the row would freeze at its first measurement (measured while building the fix: unit and real-DOM mutation, the row stays at its first value). That guard is correct, and it is exactly what leaves the items ragged: uniform pitch, non-uniform items.

Fixed mode has no such split — `style.height = owner.itemHeight` makes item, slot and (through the consumer's `height: 100%`) surface one thing. Measured mode needs the same equality without that trap.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/list/plugin/Animate.mjs`: `createItem` (the mode branch), `measureItems` → `owner.getDomRect(ids)` over the item ids, token-fenced; `rowHeight` getter; `repositionItems`.
- `src/main/DomAccess.mjs`: `getBoundingClientRect`, `getLayoutRect` — neither answers "how tall would this element be if its inline height were released".
- `DomAccess.measure({id, value})` is the nearest sibling and the placement precedent (the main thread answering a size the worker cannot compute), but it answers a different question: it converts one CSS **length** to px for one node — `%` as a fraction of the `offsetParent`'s height, any other unit through an off-screen measuring `div` — for `component.Base#measure` (the floating/align path, its only caller). It never reads an element's own natural size, it is single-node where this read must batch (release all → read all → restore all, or it thrashes layout per item), and its two branches already measure different axes. Overloading it (`value: 'auto'`) would inherit that ambiguity; the new read sits beside it instead.
- Consumers size the surface off the item: the roster's `> .fm-agent-card {height: 100%}`, the list example's cards.

## The Fix — options, each with its falsifier

| Option | Shape | Falsifier |
|---|---|---|
| **A — measure the content, size the slot** | measure each item's content element (component lists: the item component's root) and write `height: rowHeight` on the `li` | the content must then NOT stretch to the `li` (`height: 100%` re-arms the trap), so an equal-height *surface* has to be painted by the `li` — every consumer restyles, selection and focus rings included |
| **B — a natural-height read in one main-thread task** | a `DomAccess` read that releases the inline height of the given elements, reads their rects and restores it inside one task (release all → read all → restore all: one forced layout for any number of items, no painted intermediate frame); the plugin then writes `height: rowHeight` on every item, as fixed mode does | cost at a few hundred items; an item whose own CSS transitions `height` |
| **C — CSS variable + `min-height`** | publish the row height on the list root, items take `min-height: var(…)` | the measured element includes its `min-height`: grow-only by construction |

Recommendation: **B.** It keeps fixed mode's consumer contract (item = slot = surface) so a consumer switches modes by config alone, and the trap is closed where it lives — in the read.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behaviour | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.list.plugin.Animate` measured mode — item height | `Animate.mjs#createItem`, `#measureItems` (read at `dev@70c2c94618`) | every item carries `height: rowHeight` once measured; before the first measurement it stays hidden and height-less, as today | fixed mode unchanged | the `measureItemHeight_` member doc; `examples/list/animate` | unit arms: equal item heights after a settle; a row that grew shrinks back when its tall item leaves |
| `Neo.main.DomAccess.getNaturalRect` (+ the `component.Base#getNaturalRect` shortcut, beside `getLayoutRect`) — the LAYOUT box, so the answer can be written back as a CSS length | `DomAccess.mjs` remote-method list (`getBoundingClientRect` is the sibling) | for the given ids: release the named inline properties (`properties`, default `['height']`), read their layout boxes, restore the values with their priority — one task | callers that never pass it are untouched | method JSDoc | component-tier arm (a real DOM): the element's inline height and its priority are identical before and after, the returned height is its content's |

Behaviour change since `#18604` (shipped 2026-09-14, one example consumer): measured items were content-height; they become row-height.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In measured mode every rendered item has the same height, equal to `rowHeight`, after each settle pass.
- [ ] The row still shrinks: when the tallest item leaves or shortens, the next measurement publishes the smaller height (red-first against a written-height implementation without the natural read).
- [ ] No frame paints a released height (the read is one main-thread task).
- [ ] Fixed mode is byte-identical in behaviour; the `#18604` token fence still drops a stale read.
- [ ] `examples/list/animate` "Measured rows" renders equal cards in the browser, through filter and mode switches; mixed content is witnessed on a real DOM in the component tier (the example's cards share one natural height).

## Out of Scope

Per-row heights (each row as tall as its own tallest item) — a different geometry (cumulative `y`), worth its own ticket if a consumer needs it. Variable item widths.

## Avoided Traps

Writing the measured height back without changing the read (the row freezes at its first measurement). A hidden clone per item to measure (doubles the DOM and drifts from the real item's container queries — the roster card is `container-type: inline-size`).
